_readme: THE APPLY ORDER OF supabase/migrations/**. This is the single source of truth
for rebuilding the database from the repo, and it is verified on every push by
tests/schema-drift.mjs (via tests/schema-replay.mjs).
WHY THIS FILE HAS TO EXIST. Filename order does NOT replay. Measured
2026-08-14: applying supabase/schema.sql + every migration in filename order
gets 23 of 41 files in and fails the other 18. Two reasons, both structural:
1. '2026-08-08-clan-seat-2.sql' sorts BEFORE '2026-08-08-clan-seat.sql',
because '-' (0x2D) < '.' (0x2E). The -2 file's first act is to check that
clan_board exists and raise if it does not, so it fails first, every time.
2. Nine files are dated 2026-08-11 and alphabetical order puts 'accrual',
'accrue-gate', 'anon-execute-lockdown', 'apply-engine' and
'authenticated-surface-lockdown' all BEFORE 'player-state' â€” which is the
foundation every one of them depends on. There is no naming scheme that
rescues this after the fact.
Before this file, the working order existed only as a hand-maintained const
array inside tests/pglite-chain.mjs and another inside
tests/conservation-fuzz.mjs, each covering a DIFFERENT SUBSET of the
migrations, and neither one covering all of them. That means the order
required to rebuild the database was not written down anywhere.
RULES:
Â· Every .sql file in supabase/migrations/ must appear exactly once, across
'pre_schema', 'order' and 'excluded'. The guard FAILS on a file that is in
none of them â€” so a new migration cannot be silently left out of the
rebuild. The full apply sequence is: pre_schema, then supabase/schema.sql,
then order.
Â· A new migration goes where it actually has to run, not where its date
puts it.
Â· 'excluded' is a claim that a rebuilt database is CORRECT without the file.
Never add one to make the chain go green.

market_wipe_ok: read by 2026-08-17-market-v2.sql, which is in 'order'

_pre_schema_why: supabase/schema.sql creates game_saves and game_events with `create table if
not exists` as a bootstrap fallback, and its own header says they are assumed
to already exist. Those fallback definitions do not match production: different
primary key on game_saves, different COLUMN NAMES on game_events (kind vs
event_type, created_at vs occurred_at). Running the true shapes first makes
schema.sql's fallback no-op on a rebuild exactly as it no-ops on production.
The alternative â€” ALTER + rename the columns afterwards â€” is a rename on the
table holding every player's save, which cannot be rolled forward past a
failure. Ordering is reversible; that is not.

_order_notes.2026-08-30-bounty-kill-credit.sql: P0 (live, Paione): a bounty hits its target on the client but NEVER completes — hangs forever on 'completing in a moment'. Live combat is client-predicted; the server bounty counter (player_progress ev:kill_monster:<target>) is written ONLY by the away/span-sim, which re-simulates the window as an UNATTENDED character and realizes 60-99% FEWER kills than the attended player, so hr_claim_bounty's current>=required is never met and the two-phase claim (gated on the next kill) dead-ends when the player stops. Adds public.hr_credit_kills__ungated + the rate-gated hr_credit_kills wrapper (authenticated-only; hr_engine + inner shut out) that TOPS UP the counter to the client's observed kills, CLAMPED to a physical-max plausibility cap = floor(1.3 x elapsed_since_accept_ms / min_time_to_kill), with elapsed from now()-active_bounty.accepted_at (server clock), dmgLevel=greatest(str,ranged,magic) from player_skills, and hp from hr_bounty_monsters — all server-owned, no client value trusted. Cap math lives in src/core/kill-time.js (dual-runtime source of truth) and is bound to the SQL by tests/kill-time-drift.mjs. Credit is PROGRESS-ONLY (zero gold/XP/drops — three disjoint writers: credit->counter, turn-in->bounty reward once, settle->per-kill loot); the bounty reward still pays once via the unchanged hr_claim_bounty. Idempotent via advisory xact lock + FOR UPDATE on active_bounty + hr_kill_credit_log(user,slot,idem); throttled claims (credit<claimed) journalled kind='bounty' intent='kill_credit_throttled:<target>' as a forgery signal. Patches hr_rpc_gate (bucket hr_credit_kills, 60/min — unknown bucket fails closed). MUST run AFTER 2026-08-23-bounty-monsters.generated.sql (needs the hp column; §0 fails closed if absent), after 2026-08-23-bounty.sql (active_bounty + hr_claim_bounty) and after the current hr_rpc_gate last toucher. NO edge redeploy — hr_credit_kills is a standalone client RPC (supabase.rpc); client files (legacy.js credit-then-claim + Decision-1 display, goal-claim.js transport, core/kill-time.js) carry the bump. Security: GO-WITH-CONDITIONS (self-only; forged p_claimed clamped to wall-clock-bounded ~physical-max; residual = self-minting one's OWN gold+marks bounty rewards at ~legit-max rate, journalled beyond 1.3x, never crosses to another player; bounded self-only kill-stat over-count that does NOT reach leaderboards — both tracked follow-ups). Reversibility: additive — drop the two functions + hr_kill_credit_log and re-apply the hr_rpc_gate last toucher. §6 PROVES on apply, in a rolled-back subtransaction: premature claim incomplete -> credit -> claim completes and pays once; replay idempotent; cap throttles a 999-claim at ~0 elapsed to 0 (journalled); the credit grants zero gold; the turn-in pays exactly one bounty_turnin ledger row; grant/policy hygiene (no execute on __ungated/cap-fn/log for authenticated/anon, no client write on the log or player_progress).
_order_notes.2026-08-24-combat-style.sql: P0 (live, player report — Paione): 'when training combat, Strength/Defense/HP exp is not saving; only Attack saves'. supabase/functions/hr-accrue/accrual.js settled every combat window with resolveStyle(eq.weaponType, null) — null makes resolveStyle fall to the FIRST key of the weapon family, sword.accurate, which routes 100% of styled XP to ATTACK — because the player's chosen style had no server home: it lived in the save blob, then in the client_state RESIDUE bag, which is self-only and which the server is forbidden to read for authority. Skills are server-of-record and ARMED, so each settle retired the client's predicted Strength/Defence XP and wrote the Attack-only answer instead. Adds player_state.combat_style jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}' (the per-weapon-family choice map, e.g. {"sword":"defensive"}; a PARTIAL map is normal and {} means 'chosen nothing', never 'chose Accurate') with a jsonb_typeof='object' check; public.hr_combat_styles (family, style_key, is_default) seeded from src/core/styles.js COMBAT_STYLES/DEFAULT_STYLE_KEYS and bound to it in BOTH directions by tests/combat-style.mjs, carrying NOT ONE simulation number (accuracyMod/damageMod/speedMod/xp ratios stay in the one module the picker, the router and the engine all import); and hr_set_style__ungated + the rate-gated hr_set_style wrapper (authenticated-only; the inner AND hr_engine are shut out — the accrual engine reads the style and must never be able to choose which skill it pays). The caller sends a FAMILY and a KEY and nothing else, both looked up in the server catalogue; an unknown pair is REFUSED (unknown_family / unknown_style), never clamped, because a clamp would silently route XP somewhere the player did not choose — this file's own bug in miniature. Takes the SAME per-character advisory lock hr_apply takes, MERGES one key (a call about swords never resets the bow), bumps version (the column PRICES an absence — XP routing and, through speedMod, the swing interval — so an in-flight accrual must be made to re-read), and refuses mid-absence with collect_first rather than stamping accrued_to, which would confiscate the unpaid window (the hr_set_auto_eat ruling; the 60s grace mirrors ACCRUE_MIN_MS). p_idem caches the SUCCESS envelope in player_intents, read INSIDE the lock; refusals are deliberately NOT cached so a collect_first becomes retryable the moment the settle lands. It writes NO player_ledger row: the bucket is 30/min (a style flip is free and harmless by construction) and a per-gesture journal at that rate is the per-tick logging journal rule 6 forbids — if an audit trail is ever wanted, DROP THE BUCKET TO 30/HOUR FIRST. Patches hr_rpc_gate (bucket hr_set_style, 30/min — an unknown bucket fails CLOSED, so without it every call would 429) and hr_state_of (one key, 'combat_style', INSIDE the `state` object next to tool_carry/fight, because the accrual shell reads it off the row as st.combat_style) PROGRAMMATICALLY at guarded exactly-once anchors, so it carries no literal create-or-replace header for either and is a member of NO derivation chain and takes over no last-toucher role. MUST run AFTER 2026-08-26-marks-record.sql (the last STATIC hr_state_of toucher, whose 'streak_day_key' terminator is the anchor) and after every later programmatic hr_state_of patcher (bank-store, client-state, trait-buy) and after the current hr_rpc_gate last toucher (2026-08-23-trait-buy.sql). ⚠ REQUIRES AN EDGE REDEPLOY: supabase/functions/hr-accrue/accrual.js, index.ts and set-activity.js all change, and the migration alone leaves the engine still reading null. The column's PRESENCE is the switch (st.combat_style ?? null degrades to exactly the pre-migration behaviour), so the two halves are safe in either order. Reversibility: additive — drop the two functions and hr_combat_styles, optionally drop the column, and re-apply the previous hr_state_of/hr_rpc_gate last-toucher; reverting restores the bug and corrupts nothing. §8 PROVES on apply, in an HR819-rolled-back subtransaction: a fresh character projects {} (not a pre-filled default); an unknown family, an unknown style and a CROSS-FAMILY key are each refused by name and write nothing; the happy path stores the map, bumps version and reaches the envelope; a second family MERGES rather than replaces; a replay on the same idem returns the original envelope with no second version bump; a mid-absence flip is refused collect_first, writes nothing and is NOT cached; the SAME key then succeeds once the window is paid; and a second FRESH character is unaffected (the control).
_order_notes.2026-08-23-trait-buy.sql: P0 (live). src/legacy.js buyTrait() fail-closes under the LIVE marks arm ('That upgrade is unavailable right now') because NO server verb existed to debit the server-owned Bounty-Marks balance — so Auto-Eat, the purchase the death sheet teaches on a player's first death, and every other TRAIT, cannot be bought at all in production. Adds public.hr_traits (trait_id pk, currency marks|gold, cost, req_trait, auto_enable) seeded BYTE-EQUAL from src/legacy.js TRAITS (auto_eat 15 marks; auto_eat_2 100 marks req auto_eat) and bound to it in BOTH directions by tests/trait-buy.mjs, plus hr_trait_buy__ungated / the rate-gated hr_trait_buy wrapper (authenticated-only; the inner and hr_engine are shut out — the accrual engine must never buy a paid trait for anybody). The caller sends a TRAIT ID and a SLOT and nothing else: price, currency and prerequisite are read from the server catalogue, the balance from the character's own row under the SAME per-character advisory lock hr_apply takes. Refusals by name: unknown_trait / already_owned (a refusal, never a charged no-op) / requires:<id> / insufficient_marks / insufficient_gold / trait_daily_cap / bad_slot / no_character / rate_limited. p_idem caches the SUCCESS envelope in player_intents (read INSIDE the lock so two simultaneous retries cannot both miss it); refusals are deliberately NOT cached, so 'you are 5 Marks short' becomes buyable the moment the Marks arrive. Journals ONE player_ledger row kind='trait' with gold_in/xp_in/qty_in/gems_in explicitly 0 (it mints nothing) — the kind list is widened by an ANCHORED INSERTION into the live constraint rather than a restatement, so it cannot delete a kind another file added. It does NOT write player_state.auto_eat_enabled/auto_eat_pct: it writes the kind='flag' trait:<id> row and then CALLS hr_set_auto_eat, keeping that function the single writer (the whole write-clamp argument of 2026-08-29-auto-eat-tiers.sql, whose GATE(e) scans every body in public, rests on it); the enable is non-fatal, so a collect_first refusal never fails a purchase. Patches hr_rpc_gate (bucket hr_trait_buy, 12/min — an unknown bucket fails CLOSED, so without it every purchase would 429) and hr_state_of (one additive top-level `traits` id array, read UNFILTERED rather than through the LIMIT-1000 progress projection, so an entitlement can never be truncated into 'you own nothing') PROGRAMMATICALLY at guarded exactly-once anchors — it carries no literal create-or-replace header for either and is therefore a member of NO derivation chain and takes over no last-toucher role. MUST run AFTER 2026-08-29-auto-eat-tiers.sql (its precondition asserts hr_auto_eat_tier + the TIERED hr_set_auto_eat body), after 2026-08-16-unlocks.generated.sql (the storable flag rows the player_progress_unlock_guard trigger polices the grant against), after 2026-08-23-bounty.sql (player_state.marks) and after 2026-08-22-companion-record.sql (the last programmatic patcher of the hr_state_of total_level anchor). NO edge redeploy — hr_trait_buy is a standalone client RPC and nothing in src/core or src/data changed. Reversibility: additive — drop the two functions and hr_traits, and re-apply 2026-08-22-companion-record.sql to restore hr_state_of without the traits key; already-written rows are ordinary kind='flag' rows hr_auto_eat_tier reads regardless. §8 PROVES on apply, in an HR819-rolled-back subtransaction: unknown trait refused; tier II without tier I refused by name and charging nothing; tier I debits exactly 15, writes the flag, reports hr_auto_eat_tier=1, switches auto-eat on at the clamped 25% ceiling; replay on the same idem returns the original envelope with no second debit; a different key for an owned trait answers already_owned; a short purchase is refused AND not cached; tier II then reports tier 2 and both ids in `owned`; exactly two ledger rows; the envelope projects both; and a second FRESH character owns nothing and is sold nothing (the control).
_order_notes.2026-08-29-daily-task-eligibility.sql: P0 (designer ruling 2026-08-23). The date-seeded daily-task shuffle had no eligibility filter on EITHER side, so a fresh account was dealt 'Craft 8 items' + 'Smith 8 items' (900 of 1300 daily gold) against zero craftable recipes at level 1 — crafting is bench-gated behind the Workshop and smithing behind the Forge, both tier-3 rooms. Adds hr_daily_task_eligible / hr_daily_task_set_caps (PURE, IMMUTABLE — the port of src/data/goal-catalogue.js dailyTaskSetIndexes) and hr_daily_task_set_for (reads caps from player_progress kind='unlock' key='room:*' + player_skills). Restates hr_claim_daily__ungated so the offer gate is the UNION of the eligible set and the raw base 3 — see the file header: the two sides read different stores for room ownership (the rooms record is DORMANT and production holds ZERO room unlock rows), and a narrower gate would refuse legitimate claims today. None of the three new functions is client-reachable; the rate-gated hr_claim_daily wrapper is untouched. Must run AFTER 2026-08-20-goal-reward-rpc-credit.sql (its precondition asserts hr_daily_task_set / hr_goal_daily_seed / hr_claim_daily__ungated exist) and after 2026-08-11-player-state.sql (player_skills). Touches none of the graded bodies (hr_apply / hr_state_of / hr_perks_of / hr_rate_gate / hr_assert_grant_hygiene), so it is on no derivation chain. Self-check sweeps 400 day keys proving (a) the SQL port equals the JS reference, (b) a FULLY UNLOCKED account is offered exactly what the raw shuffle offered — the filter is the identity there, so this is a bug fix and not a balance change — and (c) a fresh account is never offered a bench task and never a short slate. NO edge redeploy (src/data/goal-catalogue.js is not in the hr-accrue import graph; the claim path is a standalone RPC). Reversibility: re-apply goal-reward-rpc-credit §6 for the narrow gate, then drop the three functions.
_order_notes.2026-08-29-auto-eat-tiers.sql: Designer ruling 2026-08-23. The death sheet teaches 'unlock Auto-Eat' on the player's first death; Auto-Eat cost 100 Bounty Marks (~18 contracts, ~1800 kills), so the lesson named a purchase the first week could not make. Adds a 15-Mark entry tier triggering at 25% HP; the existing 100-Mark trait becomes tier II with today's settable threshold. Server-side a tier is a CEILING on player_state.auto_eat_pct (tier 1 -> 25, tier 2 -> 100), read from the kind='flag' unlock rows trait:auto_eat / trait:auto_eat_2. Adds hr_auto_eat_tier + hr_auto_eat_max_pct (neither client-reachable) and RESTATES hr_set_auto_eat to (i) gate 'enable' on owning ANY tier rather than one trait id and (ii) clamp v_pct to the ceiling AFTER the coalesce(p_pct, stored), so the null-pct path is clamped too. The clamp is on the WRITE path only, and the header derives why that is sufficient — hr_set_auto_eat is the single writer of both auto_eat_pct and auto_eat_enabled (GATE(e) re-proves it by scanning every SQL/plpgsql body in public), the engine only eats when enabled, and entitlements are monotone. That is what keeps hr_state_of — the most-restated body in the schema, with a generated derivation chain — out of this change. Must run AFTER 2026-08-15-auto-eat.sql (restates its function) and AFTER the regenerated 2026-08-16-unlocks.generated.sql (its precondition asserts the trait:auto_eat_2 catalogue row). Touches no graded body -> on no derivation chain. hr_set_auto_eat keeps its authenticated grant + its existing hr_client_rpc_baseline row (identity_args unchanged). NO edge redeploy: src/core/auto-eat.js IS in the hr-accrue bundle, but the tier helpers added to it are client-only readers — the engine's inputs (autoEatEnabled/autoEatPct) are unchanged and resolveAutoEat is untouched, so the deployed payload's BEHAVIOUR does not move. Reversibility: re-apply 2026-08-15-auto-eat.sql §2.
_order_notes.2026-08-29-bounty-first-contract.sql: Designer ruling 2026-08-23. BOUNTY_KILL_COUNTS.cull[1] = [80,120] is the board's EASY slot for a brand-new Bounty Hunter — ~100 fights before the first Mark exists, while the death sheet points at a Marks-priced trait. Ruling: 15-25 kills at Bounty-Hunter level 1, today's tier table from level 2. hr_accept_bounty__ungated does not GENERATE a contract, it CLAMPS the client's p_required into the tier range, so this moves the tier-1 FLOOR (80 -> 15) and deliberately leaves kmax at 120: lowering the ceiling would silently rewrite an honest 80-kill contract from a client whose BH level has already passed 1. The server cannot read a Bounty-Hunter level (BH xp lives in the save blob, not player_skills), so the grace is 'fewer than 3 bounty_turnin rows in the append-only player_ledger' — DERIVED (cheapest tier-1 cull xp 38, level-2 rung 83) and a deliberate SUPERSET of level 1, because a wider server range passes an honest required through unchanged while a narrower one rewrites it. Adds hr_bounty_first_contract_range + hr_bounty_first_contract (neither client-reachable) and a PARTIAL INDEX player_ledger_bounty_idx so the grace probe is not a ledger scan. Must run AFTER 2026-08-23-bounty.sql (restates hr_accept_bounty__ungated; precondition asserts it + hr_bounty_kill_range exist). Touches no graded body -> on no derivation chain; the rate-gated wrapper and its grants are untouched. Bound to src/core/bounty.js by tests/bounty-drift.mjs. NO edge redeploy — src/core/bounty.js is NOT in the hr-accrue import graph (verified by packing the function: 23 vendored core modules, bounty.js absent). Known limitation, stated in-file: hr_ledger_prune deletes rows older than 400 days, so a very old account can re-enter the grace for one tier-1 contract. Reversibility: re-apply 2026-08-23-bounty.sql §7.

2026-08-23-open-beta.sql: THE INVITE GATE BECOMES A SWITCH, AND THE SWITCH IS SET TO OFF.
Tyler is opening the beta (2026-08-23). Deleting b457's gate was the
wrong move: twenty codes are already in people's hands, 'one code = one
account' is a property several things assume, and the beta may be
re-closed at any time. So the gate becomes CONDITIONAL on a row rather
than absent, and re-closing is ONE statement:
update public.hr_settings set value = 'on' where key = 'beta_gate';
Adds public.hr_settings (RLS on, ZERO policies, zero client grants, a
per-key domain CHECK so beta_gate can only ever be 'on'/'off') seeded
beta_gate='off' ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING - a re-apply must never silently
re-open a beta somebody closed. Adds hr_beta_gate_is_open() (FAIL
CLOSED: anything it cannot prove is 'off' reads as the closed beta) and
hr_beta_signup_message() (the new copy layer; hr_beta_gate_message is
deliberately NOT restated - two files owning one `case` is a failure
this repo has already paid for).
RESTATES three b457 bodies: hr_beta_gate_reason (ONE line - the
invite_required arm now consults the switch), hr_signup_gate (adds a
per-IP codeless-signup ACCOUNT brake, 10/day, live ONLY while the gate
is open) and hr_beta_gate_on_auth_user (adds ONE arm: codeless + gate
open => allowed, journalled outcome='open'). The trigger REGISTRATION,
the operator/admin bypasses, hr_beta_code_norm's 64-char bound, the
append-only journal and claim_beta_invite's revoked grant are untouched.
RULING, asserted in both directions: a code that IS supplied is still
validated and consumed in EVERY mode - a bogus code refuses even with
the gate open, so a typo cannot silently succeed while the player's real
code sits unspent, beta_invites.used_by keeps meaning something, one
code stays one account, and the enumeration signal survives.
MUST run AFTER 2026-08-23-beta-invite-gate.sql (its §0 fails closed
without hr_beta_gate_reason / hr_signup_gate / hr_beta_code_norm / the
attached trigger) and after 2026-08-11-player-state.sql (hr_rate_ok /
hr_rate_over / hr_rate_sample_weight / hr_record_rejection). Touches
none of the graded bodies (hr_apply / hr_state_of / hr_perks_of /
hr_rate_gate / hr_assert_grant_hygiene) so it is on no derivation chain.
NO edge redeploy - nothing in the hr-accrue import graph.
Self-check (rolled-back subtransactions, net-zero, and it FORCES
enforcement with hearthrise.invite_gate_force so the postgres bypass
cannot wave the probe through): the switch flips both ways; gate ON
reproduces b457's whole refusal set including the select-into-NULL
fail-open guard; all four spellings of 'no code' (absent key, '', '   ',
null) are accepted with the gate off; a bogus code still refuses; the
10/day/IP brake bites WITH a different-IP control and does not touch a
code-bearing signup; every b457 player-facing sentence survives the
message delegation. Trigger checks 8-11 need auth.users.raw_user_meta_data
and run on the real database only - tests/open-beta.mjs adds that column
to the PGlite fixture and drives them there.
OPS (not database state, listed in §9): email confirmations ON, auth
rate limits, the before-user-created hook still registered (the account
brake lives in the hook and CANNOT live in the trigger - no client IP
exists there), anonymous sign-ins OFF.
Reversibility: the one-line UPDATE above, or re-apply
2026-08-23-beta-invite-gate.sql to restore the three bodies verbatim.
Graded by tests/open-beta.mjs + tests/beta-invite-gate.mjs.
2026-08-23-beta-invite-gate.sql: P0 ACCESS CONTROL. Enforces the closed-beta invite at ACCOUNT CREATION.
Measured on production 2026-08-23: 8 accounts, 3 consumed invites - the
gate had never been enforced anywhere. Adds an AFTER INSERT trigger on
auth.users that consumes an unused code atomically with the user row, plus
public.hr_signup_gate(jsonb) for registration as the Supabase

LAST in the order for two reasons: it reads public.hr_rate_ok (created
earlier in the chain) and it revokes claim_beta_invite, which

would have the grant put back underneath it.
Its self-check inserts probe rows into auth.users and deletes them again,
asserting auth.users and the consumed-invite count are byte-identical
afterwards. It sets hearthrise.invite_gate_force so the probe is not waved
through by the operator bypass - verified by mutation: without that line
SELF-CHECK 1 fails, and without the `used_by is null` predicate SELF-CHECK
_order_notes.2026-08-22-raid-chest-items.sql: STAGED, NOT APPLIED by the replay (the Coordinator applied it live 2026-08-22 via execute_sql + self-check). LIVE-RPC BODY CHANGE on the item surface: closes the LAST registered inventory-flip arm-blocker besides the accepted worker+doubleDrop residuals. It makes raid_claim (the Hunt weekly/solo chest) MINT the chest MATERIALS + signature into player_inventory from hr_hunt_boss_reward, alongside the b412 gold/gems credit, in BOTH the solo and clan branches — scaled exactly as raids.js chestFor+grantReward did (clan: per-material qty = greatest(1, floor(greatest(1, round(chest_mats/n_materials)) * v_scale)); sig x1 on v_sig; solo: first two of the week's boss materials at qty 1, boss picked via hr_fnv1a('hr-raid-'||week) % boss_count, byte-identical to the client rotation). It only replaces the raid_claim__ungated(text,uuid,text,integer) BODY (same b412 arity), so the A9 wrapper, the revoked-before-granted grants and the hr_client_rpc_baseline row are untouched and stay valid. Touches NO other function body → outside every hr_assert_grant_hygiene derivation chain, takes over no role. The item mint sits AFTER the same consume guard (raid_claims on-conflict-do-nothing + row_count) the gold credit does, in the SAME transaction, so a replay is refused before any credit/mint and there is NO double-mint alongside the gold path. 'raid' is already in player_ledger_kind_check (added with the b412 credit), so NO constraint widen.
